claims.text: Active learning can identify and prioritize configurations that contribute most to solid–liquid free-energy differences near melting.
Targeted configurations selected across the phase boundary can be used to train a machine-learned interatomic potential.
The trained interatomic potential will accurately predict energies and forces near melting.
The machine-learned potential will retain vibrational entropy contributions relevant to fusion.
The machine-learned potential will retain anharmonic entropy contributions relevant to fusion.
The machine-learned potential will retain electron–vibration entropy contributions relevant to fusion.
Targeted training will reduce the amount of explicit ab initio data required for free-energy calculations.
The method is applicable to pure elements.
The method is applicable to binary alloys.
The method is applicable to multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Fusion free energies will agree with explicit AIMD benchmarks within approximately 5%.
Predicted melting temperatures will agree with explicit AIMD benchmarks within approximately 5%.
Predicted vibrational entropy differences will agree with explicit AIMD benchmarks within approximately 5%.
The method will reduce computational cost by at least an order of magnitude relative to explicit AIMD free-energy workflows.
The method will reduce computational cost by at least an order of magnitude relative to TOR-TILD.
Explicit AIMD and TOR-TILD provide established free-energy baselines for elemental and binary systems.
